angle: data: the game's own data tables for morale, fatigue, rules and campaign variables, as extracted by the open-source pack-file tool (Rusted PackFile Manager). Its schema for this title has a 'patches' section whose 'lookup_hardcoded' strings list each key-value table's row keys with their in-house descriptions; the earlier pass read only the table and field names. This pass compared those lists with the same tool's schema for TOTAL WAR: WARHAMMER II and looked for values in mod pages (search summaries only) and in public dumps (none reachable). Definitions are CODE; no value of the reference was obtained.

claims.label: CODE
claims.claim: This title's battle-morale constants (its morale key-value table: 129 row keys, each with an in-house description) describe morale as computed from a starting point plus situational effects, with the current value moving toward the computed one each tick. None of the 129 keys describes a cost for entering a battle or for time spent in one: every effect names a situation (own losses, contact direction, flanks, enemy numbers, nearby routs, fear and terror, missile and artillery fire, fatigue state, surprise, night unpreparedness, the general's presence, death or flight, terrain and fortification, winning or losing a fight, the army near destruction, pending reinforcements). Apart from the starting point itself, the only terms that apply to every unit of a side whatever the situation are a morale modifier per difficulty level, one set for the player's units and one for the AI's.

claims.notes: What this is: the tool's schema has a 'patches' section whose 'lookup_hardcoded' strings list a key-value table's row keys with a description each. The packed game table holds only 'key' and 'value' (line 199), so the descriptions come from another source of the developer's, INFERRED to be the title's Assembly Kit raw data (an Assembly Kit was released, official-38). Faithfulness INFERRED from: in-house typos kept ('minimium', 'mulitplied', 'casulties', 'timout', 'neightbouring'); title-only keys in the same lists ('troy_savage_roar_morale_amount', Aristeia and Rage keys, 'troy_mth_*'); and per-title differences against a sibling's list (data-21). Labelled CODE because these are definitions read in a faithful extraction of the game's data; if the schema is held to be only a fetched page, every CODE claim here becomes FETCH with the same verbatim quotes. NO VALUE is in the file: a defined key may be zero or unused in this title. Absence of an entry-cost key is evidence, not proof: hardcoded engine behaviour (one description says a range is 'hardcoded', data-04), campaign effects carried in as bonus values or effect bundles (data-15, data-20) and fatigue-effect rows (data-07) are outside this table. The one data path by which time in a battle could lower morale without losses is fatigue: activity deltas, including 'ready;;;;;unit in combat ready pose' and idle (data-17), feed fatigue states that carry morale concerns (data-07); whether standing ready tires or rests a unit is a value question (unknown). The file writes an apostrophe as \'.

claims.label: CODE
claims.claim: The terms that can act before any loss are conditions, not a charge for taking part: a timed 'Surprised' concern; 'Unprepared for night battle'; the fatigue concerns (data-07); one or both flanks exposed, or all secure (data-04); enemy numbers nearby; being uphill of all enemies; defending a fort or the central plaza; a bonus for pending reinforcements. claims.label: CODE
claims.claim: Casualties enter morale through three windows of the unit's own losses: the last 4 seconds (thresholds 6, 10, 15, 33 and 50 %), the last 60 seconds (10, 15, 33, 50 and 80 %) and the total (10 to 90 % in steps of 10). A separate threshold on losses in the last 4 seconds triggers a 'morale shock', and a switch chooses hit points or men as the measure. Each threshold is its own key, so the penalty is a step function of the loss share.

claims.label: CODE
claims.claim: The campaign variables carry a complete army-level ('military force') morale family of 36 keys. It has a starting value, a minimum and a maximum, and 'low' and 'very low' thresholds. It has a bonus for winning a battle, lasting a number of turns and falling off with the armies' relative strength, and a penalty for losing one, also lasting a number of turns. Other terms cover casualties, decimation, the faction leader's death, foreign soil, idleness, being led by the faction leader, looting, raiding, releasing captives, transfers, bankruptcy and attrition, plus a morale-based rebellion and the sibling's 'Waaagh'. A separate table maps a campaign group and a level key to an effect bundle. All of it is inherited: the same 36 keys with the same texts are in WARHAMMER II's list. Whether this title uses any of it is NOT established.

claims.label: CODE
claims.claim: A battle's result feeds the campaign through data-defined channels. There is experience per result type, and experience bonuses for capturing a key building or the victory location, being first into an enemy fort, and killing the enemy commander (a base plus an amount per command star), faction leader or family member. Captive options are set per campaign group, each with an effect bundle lasting a number of turns and a resource transaction. Captives can replenish between a minimum and a maximum share of the army, set by difficulty. Loot comes as a share of a routed unit's recruitment cost, scaled by casualties, and from killed agents; looted pooled resources are set per group. There is a chance to steal an item, by victory grade and higher if its holder is wounded, and interfaction loyalty by eight result grades: heroic, decisive, close and pyrrhic victory; valiant, close, decisive and crushing defeat.
